title: Reading M3 — What’s Going On in Classrooms These Days?
author: C·E·L Mathayom

slides.title: What’s Going On in Classrooms These Days?
slides.notes: Hook. Ask: How well do students behave in your class? Is it the students, the parents or the school? We will read a real news survey and decide together.

slides.title: Why is this lesson important?
slides.body:
• Classroom harmony has broken down badly in recent years.
  • Many teachers are quitting because of this.
  • What does the evidence say?
  • We will read, discuss and write.
slides.notes: Frame in real-world outcomes. Do not list grammar objectives.

slides.title: What do you already know?
slides.body:
Tell your partner what you know about this topic.

Who is to blame: students, parents or schools?

Position — Reason — Evidence — Position
slides.notes: Pair talk 1-2 min. The yellow line previews the PREP structure they will use at the end.

slides.title: Your reading mission
slides.body:
You will read 4 chunks on your handout.

Work in a team of four. Take turns. Use the four roles.
slides.notes: Set up groups of 4. Hand out the reading and the four role cards.

slides.title: How one round works
slides.body:
1. Predict — only the Predictor speaks.

2. Read the chunk silently.

3. Clarify, Question, Summarise — in turn.

4. Rotate roles. Next chunk.
slides.notes: Walk the round: Predict before reading, everyone reads silently, then the three after-roles speak in turn, then rotate.

slides.title: Your four roles
slides.body:
Predict before you read. The others talk after you read.

PredictorLook at the heading. Guess the topic.“The heading says… so I think…”
ClarifierSay what confused you. Fix it together.“I didn’t understand when it said…”
QuestionerAsk a real “I wonder…” question.“I wonder… why…”
SummariserSay the main idea in one sentence.“The main point is…”
slides.notes: Recap the four roles with the exact definitions and sentence starters. The Predictor works before reading; the other three build on each other after reading.

slides.title: Go at your own speed
slides.body:
Your team decides the pace.

Do not rush. Talk about each chunk.
slides.notes: No timer. Groups read and discuss at their own pace.

slides.title: Read Chunks 1–4
slides.body:
Work as a team of four.

Each person takes a role. Rotate for each chunk.
slides.notes: Release the reading. Circulate and prompt only where a group is stuck. Remind groups to rotate roles for each chunk.

slides.title: Write your opinion
slides.body:
Do you agree that classroom harmony is breaking down? If so, who is to blame? Students, parents or schools?

PositionI agree or I disagree.
ReasonOne reason is…
EvidenceThe text says…
PositionSo I agree or disagree.

Position — Reason — Evidence — Position
slides.notes: Use the PREP structure. The Evidence row must come from the four chunks they just read.

slides.title: Feedback before your exam
slides.body:
Write your opinion paragraph after class.

You will get grammar feedback on the class website.

Check it before your writing exam next week.
slides.notes: Explain the feedback loop: submit the paragraph, get grammar feedback on the class website, review it before the writing exam.
